3.  24-55983  Recommendation to receive and file updates from the Mayor’s Fund and Policy
  Subcommittee and the Continuum of Care (CoC) HSAC representative.

  Mayor's Fund Updates
  • Member Kimberly Lewis provided an update, there was no meeting for the
  month of December due to quorum issues.
  • The committee raised questions to clarify details in the Mayor's Fund report.
  Staff provided the necessary information to address these questions and
  clarify the report.
  Policy Subcommittee
  • Member Sarah Bedy provided an update, the subcommittee continues to
  work with staff around clean sweeps transfer cost opportunity, MHALA tour
  summary was provided and members and staff had a discussion around
  winter shelter updates.
  CoC Updates
  • Member Kimberly Lewis provided an update on the last CoC Board meeting
  which included updates on the Point-in-Time count, Proposition 1 Housing
  initiatives, Staff updates, safe sleep, Built for Zero framework and winter
  shelter updates.

  A motion was made by Member Bedy, seconded by Voting Member Killion, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  8  Bedy, Chotiswatdi, Howat, Lewis, Lie, Killion, Wood, Scott
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 3  Rew, Russell, Hilliard

  • Member Kimberly Lewis presented, the SOP is the initial document that will

5.  24-55985  Recommendation to receive and file the Homeless Services Bureau Staff
  Operations and Updates Report by Paul Duncan from the Health Department.

  A motion was made by Member Howat, seconded by Voting Member Killion,
  to approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  8  Bedy, Chotiswatdi, Howat, Lewis, Lie, Killion, Wood, Scott
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 3  Rew, Russell, Hilliard

  • Bureau Manager Paul Duncan provides staff updates and operation updates,
  which include the two city applications submitted to the state for Proposition
  1 projects at the MSC and 702 Anaheim shelter.
  • The Long Beach Homeless Coalition hosted the annual homeless memorial
  at Forest Lawn on December st.
  • As of January 1st there are now 40 additional beds at 702 Anaheim shelter,
  the MSC has activated for inclement weather shelter due to the fires.
  • The city has reached capacity for volunteers for this years homeless count.
  • HUD released the 2024 Annual Homelessness Assessment Report showing
  and 18% increase in homelessness nationwide.
  • Committee members asked staff to consider opening the winter shelter a
  month earlier.
  • A member of the public provided a comment concerning the older adults that
  are not counted because they are couch surfing or renting a room.

6.  24-56000  Recommendation to receive and file the Built for Zero Fall 2024 Learning Session
  presentation by Paul Duncan from the Health Department.

  • Bureau Manager Paul Duncan provided an overview on the Built for Zero
  conference.
  • Built for Zero is hosted by community solutions a nonprofit that was founded
  in 2011. They work with communities to implement methodologies to better
  understand the flow of people experiencing homelessness.
  • Kaiser Permanente has agreed to pay the one-time fee for any California
  community looking to join for Built for Zero.
  • Health Department staff Hannah Whitfield shared updates on the Journey so
  far, as well as outcomes from the 2024 workshop in Minneapolis.
  • Looking ahead, the goal is to reduce Long Beach’s Chronic Homelessness
  population by 10% by the next Learning session in November 2025. This can
  be achieved by focusing on improving quality data, enhancing system
  collaboration, and boosting literacy among service providers and
  governmental partners.
  • Staff encouraged committee members and members of the public to be an
  advocate for innovation and adaptability within the system, share information
  about community organizations and housing opportunities.
